title: Red-cell distribution width did not establish incremental FEV1 prediction across two NHANES samples
abstract: Fixed models trained in 2,258 NHANES 2007–2008 adults were evaluated in 2,478 separate 2009–2010 adults. Adding RDW to demographic, body-size, smoking, hemoglobin, MCV and WBC predictors changed examination-weighted FEV1 mean squared error by -0.00034694 L² (conditional Rao–Wu PSU-bootstrap95% interval -0.00094351 to +0.00035728). RMSE changed from 0.445359 to 0.444969 L; the prespecified improvement criterion failed. A flexible spline baseline nearly eliminated the point gain. Author arithmetic checks and a clean offline rerun passed. These are separate survey samples with shared infrastructure and no definitive cross-cycle person linkage, not independent-institution validation. No new RDW–lung association, equivalence, causal effect or clinical utility is claimed.
